subject.title: fix(cli): reject unknown models in config set

question: Should `openclaw config set` reject a changed text-model reference whenever its current provider catalog/auth context cannot resolve it, instead of preserving the historical write-now and fail-later runtime behavior?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and operator-experience choice, not a mechanically provable defect: the branch changes when users learn about unresolved models and can block writes that previously succeeded.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed validation
options.body: Approve the branch’s immediate rejection policy so invalid or unresolved changed text-model references cannot be persisted through `config set`.

options.title: Preserve deferred writes
options.body: Request a redesign that preserves the existing write behavior and provides a separate validation or doctor path rather than blocking `config set`.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed validation
recommendation.body: Approve the branch’s immediate rejection policy so invalid or unresolved changed text-model references cannot be persisted through `config set`.

likelyOwner.reason: Their member comment specifically identifies the unresolved compatibility choice and the absence of a safe mechanical repair.
